children: The €56 bln French bank is among Europe’s lowest-valued lenders. It expects cost cuts, AI savings, and an efficient digital to lift returns above 15% by 2030. Rivals are further ahead. At least CEO Slawomir Krupa doesn’t need rosy revenue growth or high rates to boost the shares.
Full view will be published shortly.
Société Générale on September 12 announced targets for 2029, pledging a higher return on equity.

The bank run by Slawomir Krupa now expects a return on tangible equity of 13-14% by 2029, and over 15% by 2030. It expects to achieve that thanks to revenue growth of around 3% per year, and cutting costs to less than 55% of revenues in 2029.
Société Générale shares were up some 2.7% at 74.58 euros as of 1042 GMT on September 12.
